name: Question 12
problem:
Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field
$F(x,y)=3({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,i-6xy\,j?$
worked_solution:
A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that $F(x,y)=3({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,i-6xy\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)=3({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})$ and $Q(x,y)=-6xy.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=6x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-6x.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=6x+(-6x)=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=3({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}),\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=6xy.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=0,$ and $g(y)=-{y}^{3},$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}.
$$

html:
Question 12
?

Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field F(x,y)=3(x2−y2)i−6xyj?

a
ψ(x,y)=2xy3
b
ψ(x,y)=3x2y−xy2
c
ψ(x,y)=x2y2
d
ψ(x,y)=x3y
e
ψ(x,y)=3x2y−y3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A vector field F=Pi+Qj with a simply connected domain D⊆R2 has a stream function ψ(x,y) if and only if ∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Note that F(x,y)=3(x2−y2)i−6xyj is a vector field with simply connected domain D=R2, where P(x,y)=3(x2−y2) and Q(x,y)=−6xy. Computing the partial derivatives, we have

∂P∂x=6x,∂Q∂y=−6x.

Hence, F has a stream function, since

∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=6x+(−6x)=0.

Next, we find a stream function. A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x.

In our case, we have

∂ψ∂y=3(x2−y2),∂ψ∂x=6xy.

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

ψ(x,y)=3x2y−y3+f(x),ψ(x,y)=3x2y+g(y)

where f and g are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting f=0, and g(y)=−y3, we have

ψ(x,y)=3x2y−y3.
